native_interfaces.semantics_assumed: The active init/update/finalize path returns the standard BLAKE3 extendable-output hash of exactly the supplied bytes; a 32-byte request returns the standard 256-bit digest. The FFI respects Lean ownership, lifetime, array-size, and C-ABI contracts. Uncalled keyed, derive-key, and version exports are covered because importing Blake3.Rust makes them reachable to downstream Lean code, but Compilatr.ix does not currently rely on their results. The sibling Blake3.C module binds the vendored C implementation behind six c_blake3_* externs; Compilatr.ix does not import it, so they are inventoried as present-but-unimported and any drift in the package tree's extern set fails the check.
native_interfaces.proof_effect: Content addresses use this result operationally. There is no Lean theorem connecting the returned bytes to a pure BLAKE3 specification, so collision resistance and conformance are explicit assumptions rather than proved facts. Generic evaluator readdressing, HPT evaluator and case-binder-field concretization, owner-sensitive case pruning, exact scalar fetch forwarding, local PAP/application refinement, and the rooted-restriction fuel induction are hash-independent and remain in the ordinary logical axiom set, while the indexed production addressed-lowering, checked HPT cache/summary/accepted-result/consumer theorem cones, and public reachability theorems that validate an exact input digest intentionally expose Blake3.HasherOps.hash._native.native_decide.ax_1✝ because they consume actual native digests; Compilatrix/Fence.lean pins that exact exception. The opaque FFI declarations also cross a proof-bearing subtype boundary for output length.

native_interfaces.semantics_assumed: On the x86_64-linux baseline, a successful regular-file call has opened a non-symlink regular file, completed fsync, and closed its descriptor; a successful directory call has done the corresponding type-checked fsync for the directory entry set. EINTR is retried. On Apple platforms the regular-file path first requests F_FULLFSYNC and falls back to fsync only when that operation is unsupported; directories use fsync. In every case the filesystem, kernel, and storage device truthfully implement the successful synchronization result, and the shim obeys Lean's borrowed-string and IO-result ABI.
native_interfaces.proof_effect: This boundary affects cache publication durability and availability only. Persisted HPT records remain untrusted bytes and cross the same bounded decoder, address checks, and ordinary certificate checker on every read, so no theorem or accepted compilation result assumes that sync succeeded semantically. A malicious shim could still corrupt arbitrary process state or filesystem data because it is native code.

seed_and_build_trust.current_role: The upstream Lean compiler, elaborator, kernel, interpreter, code generator, and runtime build Compilatr.ix, check proof terms, execute elaboration-time guards, and host the compiled test executable.
seed_and_build_trust.assumption: The pinned seed accepts and executes the checked sources according to Lean 4 semantics and its runtime ABI. Kernel checking narrows ordinary proof trust, but a compromised compiler/runtime can still falsify executable guards or binaries and is the bootstrap seed addressed by diverse double compilation.
seed_and_build_trust.trust_basis: lean-toolchain pins leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0; lean4-nix and nixpkgs resolution are locked by flake.lock.
seed_and_build_trust.retirement: Gen 1 self-hosting plus address-exact diverse double compilation; production proof checking then moves to the independently specified public lean4ix/ix verified checker.

seed_and_build_trust.current_role: A direct Nix build input and part of the Lean runtime's arbitrary-precision arithmetic implementation; it is not called through a project-defined Lean @[extern].
seed_and_build_trust.assumption: GMP arithmetic and memory behavior are correct when the seed/runtime evaluates large natural and integer computations, including executable validators and guards.
seed_and_build_trust.trust_basis: pkgs.gmp comes from locked nixpkgs revision 1306659b587dc277866c7b69eb97e5f07864d8c4; the x86_64-linux closure currently resolves gmp-6.3.0 and gmp-with-cxx-6.3.0.
seed_and_build_trust.retirement: Post-M3 verified limb bignums: refinement proofs against Nat/Int, backend compilation in the no-runtime fragment, and no GMP path in the self-hosted runtime closure.

seed_and_build_trust.current_role: The pinned Lean seed, generated test executable, Rust BLAKE3 static library, and project durable-sync shim execute against the host C ABI/runtime. The sync boundary directly uses open, fstat, fsync, and close. The baseline closure also contains libgcc 14.3.0 and compiler-rt 21.1.2.
seed_and_build_trust.assumption: C ABI calls, allocation, memory copying, process startup, and the host facilities used transitively by Lean/Rust behave correctly.
seed_and_build_trust.trust_basis: Linux runtime artifacts come from the locked nixpkgs closure; Darwin necessarily uses the corresponding Nix SDK/system boundary and is not claimed by the Linux version string.
seed_and_build_trust.retirement: Gen 1 removes the upstream runtime; later runtime milestones replace allocator/memcpy and the libc surface with verified .ix code plus an explicitly axiomatized syscall boundary.

seed_and_build_trust.current_role: Nix, nixpkgs, lean4-nix, flake-parts, crane, fenix/Rust, Clang/LLD, rsync, and the configured binary cache construct the Lean and Rust artifacts and run all checks.
seed_and_build_trust.assumption: Nix evaluates and realizes the locked derivations faithfully; compilers, linkers, builders, and fetched sources match their content hashes. The argumentcomputer Cachix key is trusted for signed substitution, with Nix store hashes still fixing content.
seed_and_build_trust.trust_basis: Every flake node has a locked revision/narHash and the complete lockfile hash is checked by the ledger validator.
seed_and_build_trust.retirement: This is build/supply-chain trust rather than a target-language extern. It shrinks through reproducible bootstrap artifacts and diverse reproduction; it leaves the semantic TCB when Gen 1 artifacts are address-exactly reproduced by an independent path.

seed_and_build_trust.current_role: Checks out the repository, installs Nix, and invokes nix flake check. It does not replace local reproduction of the pinned Nix derivations.
seed_and_build_trust.assumption: GitHub reports the workflow result honestly and supplies the pinned action revisions; the runner image itself is mutable.
seed_and_build_trust.trust_basis: Third-party actions are pinned by full commit and checked against this ledger; Nix then rebuilds or hash-verifies the actual project closure.
seed_and_build_trust.retirement: No semantic retirement required. For release attestation, reproduce the locked flake outside GitHub and compare store/output hashes.
